en: to be ended; to be finished; to be ruined

examples.ko: 이번 시험을 망치면 내 성적은 끝장나요.
examples.en: If I mess up this exam, my grades are done for.
The relationship between the two ended that very day.

examples.ko: 이대로 가면 우리 회사가 끝장날지도 몰라요.
examples.en: If we keep going like this, our company might be finished.

examples.ko: 저 가게는 장사가 안 돼서 곧 끝장날 것 같아요.
examples.en: That shop isn't doing well and seems about to go under.

examples.ko: 다 끝장났다고 생각했는데 다시 기회가 왔어요.
examples.en: I thought it was all over, but another chance came.

examples.ko: 그 소문이 퍼지면 그 사람 인생은 끝장날 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If that rumor spreads, that person's life could be ruined.

explain: '끝나다'보다 훨씬 강하게, 더 이상 가망이 없이 망한다는 부정적인 느낌이에요. 관계, 사업, 계획이 완전히 무너질 때 구어로 많이 써요. 일상적인 일이 단순히 끝나는 것에는 '끝나다'를 써야 해요.

phrases.en: I broke my promise, so our relationship is over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 이미 완전히 망했다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form saying it's already completely ruined.

phrases.en: At this rate, my business will be finished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 망할 것 같다는 걱정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses worry that something is about to be ruined.

phrases.example: 시험에서 떨어져서 인생이 끝장나는 줄 알았어요.
phrases.en: I failed the exam and thought my life was over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실은 그렇지 않았지만 그때는 그렇게 느꼈다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you felt that way then, though it wasn't actually true.

explain_en: Spoken, negative; a relationship or situation collapses (사이가 끝장나다). It is much stronger than '끝나다' and carries a negative sense of something being ruined beyond hope. In speech it is used when a relationship, business, or plan completely collapses. For things that simply finish, use '끝나다'.

t90.ax: If I mess up this exam, my grades are done for.

en: to be forced out; to be driven out; to be expelled

examples.ko: 그는 집세를 못 내서 집에서 내쫓겼어요.
examples.en: He couldn't pay the rent and was kicked out of his house.
The stray cat keeps getting chased away from in front of the shop.
I'm anxious that I might be pushed out of the company.
I broke a promise and ended up being kicked out of the group.
I ended up in a situation of being thrown out by the owner.
I was suddenly thrown out and had nowhere to go.

explain: '내쫓다'(몰아내다)의 피동이에요. '집에서 내쫓기다'처럼 장소는 '-에서', 내쫓은 사람은 '-에게'로 말해요. '쫓겨나다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: I got kicked out of the restaurant for being noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내쫓기다'와 비슷한 뜻이고 일상에서 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '내쫓기다' and more common in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 어릴 때 집에서 내쫓겼어요.
phrases.en: That child was driven out of the house when young.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에서'로 장소를 붙여 어디에서 쫓겨났는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-에서' to say the place someone was driven out of.
phrases.en_equiv: to be driven out of one's home

phrases.en: I felt bad because I was thrown out of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유나 이어지는 상황을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for giving a reason or continuing the situation.

explain_en: Passive, everyday; someone is chased out of a place. It is the passive of '내쫓다' (to drive out). The place takes '-에서' and the person who drove you out takes '-에게', as in '집에서 내쫓기다'. '쫓겨나다' is used with a similar meaning.

t90.ax: I was suddenly thrown out and had nowhere to go.

en: to prepare; to be ready; to guard against

examples.en: I prepare for the chance of rain.
I study every day to prepare for the exam.
There was a drill to prepare for earthquakes.
I bought clothes in preparation for winter.
To prepare for later, you have to save.
I'll be ready for the worst case.

explain: '대비하다'는 일어날지 모르는 일을 미리 준비할 때 써요. '준비하다'는 해야 할 일을 갖추는 것이고, '대비하다'는 나쁜 일이나 변화에 맞서 갖추는 것이에요. 보통 '~에 대비하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: If you prepare ahead, you worry less.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미리'와 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with '미리' (in advance).

phrases.en: I bought thick clothes to prepare for the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 위해 준비했는지 이유를 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connects the thing you prepared for with what you did.

phrases.en: Prepare water in case of an earthquake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 해 두라고 권하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite suggestion to get ready ahead of time.

explain_en: Prepare for a possible future risk or test. 대비하다 is used when you prepare in advance for something that might happen. 준비하다 is getting ready for something you have to do, while 대비하다 is getting ready against bad events or change. It is usually '~에 대비하다'.

dis.h: prepare against a possible future risk
gh: get ready; the all-purpose everyday word

p.n: 대비하다 takes 에 and means guarding against something, while 준비하다 takes an object, so the same sentence cannot simply swap.

t90.ax: I prepare for the chance of rain.

examples.en: The hunter set a trap in the forest.

examples.ko: 작은 새가 덫에 걸려서 날지 못했어요.
examples.en: A small bird got caught in a trap and couldn't fly.
This email might be a scammer's trap.

examples.ko: 덫이 너무 튼튼해서 고양이가 빠져나오지 못했어요.
examples.en: The trap was so sturdy that the cat couldn't get out.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 덫에 빠지지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to fall into that person's trap.
Don't sign a contract that feels like a trap.

explain: 동물을 잡는 도구가 덫이고, 쥐를 잡는 것은 '쥐덫'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여요. '함정'은 구덩이 같은 느낌이 강하고, 덫은 한번 걸리면 빠져나오기 힘든 느낌이에요. '덫을 놓다', '덫에 걸리다'가 대표적이에요.

phrases.en: fall into a trap
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 아니라 사람이 남의 속임수나 나쁜 상황에 빠질 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is also used when a person, not an animal, gets caught in someone's trick or a bad situation.

explain_en: The tool that catches animals is a 덫, and you attach the target in front, as in 쥐덫 (mouse trap). 함정 feels more like a pit, while 덫 feels like something that is hard to escape once caught. Typical uses are 덫을 놓다 and 덫에 걸리다.

examples.en: The road was blocked, so I turned back.

examples.ko: 그는 문 앞에서 갑자기 되돌아서 나갔어요.
examples.en: He suddenly turned around at the door and went out.

examples.ko: 이미 너무 멀리 와서 되돌아설 수는 없어요.
examples.en: We've come too far to turn back.
The moment I was about to turn back, someone called me.
His back as he turned away looked lonely.

examples.ko: 마음을 바꿔 되돌아서면 아직 늦지 않아요.
examples.en: If you change your mind and turn back, it's not too late.

explain: '돌아서다'가 몸의 방향을 바꾸는 것이라면, '되돌아서다'는 왔던 쪽으로 다시 몸을 돌리는 느낌이 있어요. 길을 되돌아갈 때는 '되돌아가다'를 같이 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그는 잠깐 서 있다가 되돌아서서 갔어요.
phrases.en: He stood for a moment, then turned back and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되돌아서다'에 '-아서'를 붙여 방향을 바꾼 뒤 이어지는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아서 links turning back to the action that follows.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 산 중간에서 되돌아섰어요.
phrases.en: It rained a lot, so we turned back halfway up the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가던 길을 다 가지 않고 도중에 돌아올 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you don't finish the route and turn back partway.

phrases.example: 길을 잘못 들어서 왔던 길로 되돌아갔어요.
phrases.en: I took the wrong road, so I went back the way I came.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되돌아서다'는 몸을 돌리는 동작이고, '되돌아가다'는 실제로 왔던 곳으로 가는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 되돌아서다 is the turning motion; 되돌아가다 is actually going back to where you came from.

explain_en: Turning around on the spot to head back, as when a road is blocked. While '돌아서다' means simply turning around, '되돌아서다' feels like turning back toward where you came from. When you actually go back along the road, '되돌아가다' is often used alongside it.

examples.en: I secretly eavesdropped on the people next to me.

examples.ko: 남의 전화를 엿듣는 건 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: It's rude to eavesdrop on other people's phone calls.
Don't eavesdrop at the door; come in.
My younger sibling was listening in on our talk.
The conversation I overheard at the cafe was so funny.

examples.ko: 누가 엿들을까 봐 작은 목소리로 말했어요.
examples.en: I spoke quietly in case someone was listening in.

explain: 남이 모르게 몰래 듣는다는 느낌이라, 우연히 들린 것은 '듣게 되다'로 말하는 편이 자연스러워요. '듣다'처럼 ㄷ 불규칙이라서 '엿들어요', '엿들었어요', '엿들은'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: I was eavesdropping on the conversation in front of the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몰래 듣고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of secretly listening.

phrases.en: Please don't eavesdrop on other people's talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의를 지키라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to remind someone to be polite.

phrases.en: I didn't tell anyone the story I overheard.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㄷ 불규칙이라서 '엿듣다'가 '엿들은'으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a ㄷ irregular verb, 엿듣다 becomes 엿들은.

explain_en: It carries the feeling of listening secretly, so for something you just happened to hear, '듣게 되다' sounds more natural. Like '듣다' it is a ㄷ-irregular verb, giving '엿들어요', '엿들었어요' and '엿들은'.

en: to be surrounded; to be encircled; to be enveloped

examples.en: The house was surrounded by reporters.
The army was encircled by the enemy in the mountains.
The people who were surrounded waited for rescue.

examples.ko: 차에 탄 채 팬들에게 포위돼서 움직일 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Still in the car, I was surrounded by fans and could not move.
The thief gave up once the police surrounded him.
All sides were blocked, and it felt like being surrounded.

explain: 포위되다는 사방이 막혀 빠져나갈 길이 없는 상태를 말해요. 기자·팬·경찰에게 둘러싸이는 장면에 자주 써요. 쓰기는 '~에게 포위되다'예요.

phrases.en: There was no one inside the surrounded building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The village was surrounded by the enemy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않게 둘러싸였다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense that it happened against one's will.

phrases.en: The singer was surrounded by fans.
phrases.nuance_ko: '포위되다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 포위되다 and more common in daily life.

explain_en: 포위되다 is the state of being hemmed in on all sides with no way out, often in scenes of being mobbed by reporters, fans or police. The pattern is '~에게 포위되다'.

examples.en: I saw a knight's armor from long ago at the museum.
Armor is heavy, so it is hard to wear for long.

examples.ko: 영화 주인공이 은색 갑옷을 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: The hero of the movie appeared in silver armor.
The armor got dented when the sword hit it.

examples.ko: 아이가 종이로 갑옷 모양 옷을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child made an armor-shaped outfit out of paper.
It is dangerous to fight without armor.

explain: 갑옷은 '입다'와 함께 쓰고, 몸 전체를 감싸는 옛날 쇠 옷을 떠올리면 돼요. 가슴만 막는 '방탄조끼'와는 달라요. 요즘은 역사, 게임, 영화 이야기에서 주로 들어요.

phrases.example: 기사가 무거운 갑옷을 입고 말에 탔어요.
phrases.en: The knight put on heavy armor and got on the horse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑옷과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb most often used with 갑옷.

phrases.en: When the fight ended, the soldiers took off their armor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입다'의 반대 동작으로, 싸움이 끝났을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite action of '입다', often used when a fight is over.

phrases.en: A knight in armor appeared in the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 꼴로 사람을 꾸며서 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This modifier form describes how a person looks.

explain_en: 갑옷 goes with the verb 입다 and brings to mind the old metal suit that covers the whole body. It differs from a 방탄조끼 (bulletproof vest), which protects only the chest. Today you mostly hear it in talk about history, games, and movies.

examples.ko: 저는 광대뼈가 높아서 사진이 잘 나와요.
examples.en: I have high cheekbones, so I look good in photos.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 광대뼈 위에 볼터치를 해요.
examples.en: When I do makeup, I put blush on top of my cheekbones.
I fell and hurt my cheekbone.
When you smile, the cheekbone area lifts up.
He has a face with prominent cheekbones.
The cheekbone is right below the eye.

explain: 말할 때는 '광대'라고 줄여서 '광대가 나왔다'처럼 말하기도 해요. '광대뼈가 나오다', '광대뼈가 튀어나오다'처럼 얼굴 모양을 설명할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 사진을 찍으면 광대가 더 나와 보여서 고민이에요.
phrases.en: In photos my cheekbones look more prominent, which worries me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '광대뼈'를 줄여서 '광대'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, '광대뼈' is often shortened to '광대'.

phrases.en: That actor's cheekbones stick out somewhat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴 모양을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe the shape of a face.

phrases.en: I fell and hurt the cheekbone area.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쪽'을 붙이면 몸의 대략적인 위치를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '쪽' gives the rough location on the body.

explain_en: In speech people sometimes shorten it to '광대', as in '광대가 나왔다'. It often appears when describing face shape, as in '광대뼈가 나오다' or '광대뼈가 튀어나오다'.

examples.en: I didn't want to do my homework, so I pretended to be sick.

examples.ko: 꾀병인 줄 알았는데 진짜 열이 있었어요.
examples.en: I thought he was faking it, but he really had a fever.

examples.ko: 동생이 학교에 안 가려고 꾀병을 부리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling seems to be faking illness to skip school.

examples.ko: 꾀병 부리지 말고 어서 일어나서 준비해요.
examples.en: Stop faking being sick and get up and get ready.
Mom quickly figured out that I was faking.

examples.ko: 시험 날만 되면 배가 아프다니 꾀병 아니에요?
examples.en: Your stomach only hurts on exam days? Aren't you faking it?

explain: 보통 '꾀병을 부리다'로 말해요. 진짜 아픈 사람에게 '꾀병이야'라고 하면 크게 실례가 되니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 동생이 시험 날 아침에 꾀병을 부렸어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling faked being sick on the morning of the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꾀병'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb paired with '꾀병'.

phrases.en: I'm not faking it. I'm really sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 의심할 때 진짜 아프다고 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are really sick when others doubt you.

phrases.en: My younger sibling skipped school by faking illness.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙여 어떤 이유로 행동했는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-으로' you can say what the reason for an action was.
phrases.en_equiv: to be absent by faking illness

explain_en: It is usually said as '꾀병을 부리다'. Be careful: telling someone who is truly sick '꾀병이야' is very rude.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my body is shivering.
My hands trembled with fear.

examples.ko: 겨울 바람 속에서 덜덜 떨며 버스를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited for the bus, shivering in the winter wind.

examples.ko: 시험 전에는 다리가 덜덜 떨릴 만큼 긴장돼요.
examples.en: Before the exam, I'm so nervous that my legs shake.

examples.ko: 낡은 세탁기가 덜덜 소리를 내며 돌아가요.
examples.en: The old washing machine runs with a rattling noise.
He spoke while trembling.

explain: 추위나 무서움 때문에 몸이 크게 떨리는 모양이에요. 보통 '덜덜 떨다, 덜덜 떨리다'로 써요. '달달'은 더 작고 가볍게 떠는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I shivered all day because it was cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 몸을 떠는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's body is shaking.

phrases.en: My legs are trembling because I'm scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 저절로 떨리는 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the body shakes on its own.

phrases.en: The puppy is trembling after getting wet in the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '덜덜'보다 작고 가볍게 떠는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A smaller, lighter shaking than '덜덜'.

explain_en: Shaking strongly from cold or fear, heavy and continuous. It describes the body shaking hard from cold or fear, usually as '덜덜 떨다' or '덜덜 떨리다'. '달달' gives a smaller, lighter shaking feel.

en: to be thick; to be plump

examples.en: Thick socks are nice in winter.
My younger sibling has full lips, so they look cute.
This notebook has nicely thick paper.
I grilled thickly sliced meat.
The blanket is thick, so it will be warm.
The cardigan was thick but not heavy.

explain: '두껍다'는 그냥 두께가 있다는 뜻이고, '도톰하다'는 적당히 두꺼워서 따뜻하거나 보기 좋다는 느낌이 있어요. 옷, 입술, 고기, 종이에 자주 써요. 너무 두꺼울 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I bought a thick coat to wear in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도톰하다'를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 옷이나 물건의 따뜻하고 보기 좋은 두께를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun, describing the pleasantly substantial thickness of clothes or objects.

phrases.example: 이 종이는 도톰해서 잘 안 찢어져요.
phrases.en: This paper is thick, so it doesn't tear easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요. 두께 때문에 좋은 점이 있을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for giving a reason, often when the thickness brings a benefit.

phrases.example: 이 양말은 도톰하지 않아서 좀 추워요.
phrases.en: These socks aren't thick, so they feel a bit cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두께가 부족하다고 말하는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying something lacks enough thickness.

explain_en: Soft, nicely thick fabric or slices; warm feel (도톰한 양말) 두껍다 just says something has thickness, while 도톰하다 suggests it is moderately thick in a nice or cozy way. It is common for clothes, lips, meat and paper, but not for something excessively thick.

examples.en: My cold was bad, so I got an IV drip.
I fell asleep while getting the IV drip.

examples.ko: 링거 바늘을 꽂을 때 아파서 얼굴을 찡그렸어요.
examples.en: It hurt when the IV needle went in, so I frowned.
The IV bottle is almost empty.
After getting the drip, I felt energized.
The nurse swapped in a new IV bag.

explain: '링거를 맞다'라고 하고 '먹다'를 쓰지 않아요. 원래는 수액의 한 종류 이름인데 한국에서는 팔에 꽂는 수액 주사를 통틀어 '링거'라고 해요. 병원에서 쓰는 정확한 말은 '수액'이에요.

phrases.en: The nurse set up an IV drip in my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사나 간호사가 링거를 연결해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a doctor or nurse sets up the IV.

phrases.en: I lay down with an IV in my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 링거 바늘이 팔에 꽂혀 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the IV needle being in your arm.

phrases.en: I got an IV drip at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 쓰는 더 정확한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more exact word used in hospitals.

explain_en: You say '링거를 맞다', never '먹다'. It was originally the name of one type of IV fluid, but in Korea '링거' covers any IV drip into the arm. The more exact hospital term is '수액'.

examples.en: It was cold, so I wrapped a scarf around my neck.

examples.ko: 엄마가 손으로 짠 머플러를 선물해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mom gave me a scarf she knitted by hand.
In winter, just one scarf keeps you warm.

examples.ko: 이 빨간 머플러는 어느 코트에나 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This red scarf goes well with any coat.
My scarf almost blew away in the wind.
I left my scarf on the subway.

explain: 목에 두르는 목도리를 말하고, 일상에서는 '목도리'가 더 흔해요. '머플러'는 패션 쪽에서 조금 멋을 내는 느낌으로 써요. 자동차 배기 장치를 뜻하는 '머플러'도 있어서 문맥으로 구분해요.

phrases.en: I always wear a scarf in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '머플러'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서는 이 말이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 머플러 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I feel warm because I'm wearing a red scarf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목에 두르는 모습을 가볍게 말할 때 '하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 하다 as a light way to say wearing a scarf.

phrases.example: 그 코트에는 회색 머플러가 잘 어울려요.
phrases.en: A gray scarf goes well with that coat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멋을 낸 모습을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compliment someone's style.

explain_en: It means a neck scarf, but 목도리 is more common in daily life. 머플러 sounds a bit more fashionable. 머플러 can also mean a car's exhaust muffler, so context tells you which one is meant.

t90.ax: I left my scarf on the subway.
